key_concept: Fossils, homologous organs (divergent evolution) and analogous organs (convergent evolution) are accepted evidences of evolution, whereas Haeckel's embryological evidence was disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer.
steps: Option (1): Wings of birds and butterflies do the same job but have different structures and origins. They are analogous organs, produced by convergent evolution in similar habitats, so they are valid evidence of evolution.
Option (2): Fossils of different ages in rock layers show that life forms changed over time and that some became extinct. Paleontological evidence is a valid evidence of evolution.

Option (3): Ernst Haeckel pointed to features common to all vertebrate embryos, such as rudimentary gill slits, as proof that embryos recapitulate evolutionary history. Karl Ernst von Baer showed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals, so this embryological support was disapproved.

Option (4): Forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs and humans share the same basic bone plan but are modified for different functions. They are homologous organs, produced by divergent evolution from a common ancestor, so they are valid evidence of evolution.
Only option (3) is the evidence that was rejected, so it is the correct answer.
final_answer: Option (3): Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
why_not_others: Convergent evolution (analogy), divergent evolution (homology) and fossil records are all accepted evidences. Students sometimes wrongly think analogous organs cannot support evolution, but they show adaptive evolution under similar selection pressures.
common_trap: Students assume convergent evolution is 'not evidence' because analogous organs do not show common ancestry, and they miss the textbook line that Haeckel's embryological support was disapproved by von Baer.
time_saving_tip: Remember the paired fact 'Haeckel proposed, von Baer disapproved'. Any option citing Haeckel's embryological support is the 'not evidence' choice.
